about.description:
osl-dynamics is a Python toolbox for studying brain dynamics using
neuroimaging data: MEG, EEG and fMRI. It provides generative models that
decompose data into brain networks, including the Hidden Markov Model
(HMM) and Dynamic Network Modes (DyNeMo), along with data preparation,
spectral estimation, network visualisation and statistical significance
testing.
about.summary: Toolbox for studying dynamic functional brain networks in neuroimaging data

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "3.6.2"

recipe:
  name: osl-dynamics
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/o/osl-dynamics/osl_dynamics-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 9a206df17a78422d96ff75be73d0248fae059f618cefff7a49ac0942d2d3ad2b

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - package:
      name: osl-dynamics-base
    build:
      noarch: python
      python:
        entry_points:
          - osl-dynamics = osl_dynamics.config_api.pipeline:osl_dynamics_cli
          - osl-dynamics-download-data = osl_dynamics.files._fetch:download_data_cli
      script:
        env:
          SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ version }}
        content: python -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools >=77
        - setuptools_scm >=8
        - wheel
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - fslpy
        - h5io
        - h5py
        - ipyevents
        - ipywidgets
        - mat73
        - matplotlib-base
        - mne-base
        - mne-icalabel
        - onnxruntime
        - nest-asyncio2
        - nibabel
        - nilearn
        - numba
        - numpy
        - osfclient
        - packaging
        - pandas
        - pooch
        - pqdm
        - pyside6
        - pyvista
        - pyvistaqt
        - pyyaml
        - scikit-image
        - scikit-learn
        - scipy
        - seaborn
        - threadpoolctl
        - tqdm
        - trame
        - trame-vtk
        - trame-vuetify
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - osl_dynamics
            - osl_dynamics.analysis
            - osl_dynamics.config_api
            - osl_dynamics.data
            - osl_dynamics.files
            - osl_dynamics.glm
            - osl_dynamics.inference
            - osl_dynamics.meeg
            - osl_dynamics.simulation
            - osl_dynamics.utils
          pip_check: true
          # noarch, so check the oldest and the newest supported Python
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
      - script:
          - osl-dynamics --help
          - osl-dynamics-download-data --help
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*

  # As above, plus the TensorFlow stack needed to build and train models.
  - package:
      name: osl-dynamics
    build:
      # conda-forge has no TensorFlow for Windows newer than 1.14
      skip:
        - win
    requirements:
      run:
        - osl-dynamics-base ==${{ version }}
        - if: osx and x86_64
          then:
            # conda-forge's newest TensorFlow for Intel Macs. Pinning the 2.19
            # used elsewhere is not possible: it has no osx-64 build
            - tensorflow ==2.18.0
            - tensorflow-probability ==0.25.0
            - tf-keras ==2.18.0
          else:
            - tensorflow ==2.19.1
            - tensorflow-probability ==0.25.0
            - tf-keras ==2.19.0
        - if: linux and x86_64
          then:
            # software (off-screen) rendering, so that the 3D plotting works
            # on machines without a display. This is the only platform with
            # OSMesa VTK builds
            - vtk * *osmesa*
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - osl_dynamics.models
          pip_check: true

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/OHBA-analysis/osl-dynamics
  repository: https://github.com/OHBA-analysis/osl-dynamics
  documentation: https://osl-dynamics.readthedocs.io
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - NOTICE
  summary: Toolbox for studying dynamic functional brain networks in neuroimaging data
  description: |
    osl-dynamics is a Python toolbox for studying brain dynamics using
    neuroimaging data: MEG, EEG and fMRI. It provides generative models that
    decompose data into brain networks, including the Hidden Markov Model
    (HMM) and Dynamic Network Modes (DyNeMo), along with data preparation,
    spectral estimation, network visualisation and statistical significance
    testing.

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - cgohil8
